subject: CAIQ tenant-scope assertion walkthrough and evidence timeline
messages:
From: Ronald Hart <security@atlashealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ tenant scoping question and sample request

Hi Marissa / Kim,

Thanks again for taking our initial CAIQ walkthrough last week. We're preparing the detailed control mapping for our cloud tenancy and have a couple of scope clarifications before we start collecting artifacts: 

1) Tenant isolation: Atlas runs three logical tenant groups (prod, partner-sandboxes, analytics). For controls that reference environment-level telemetry and runtime logs, do you produce per-tenant log digests, or is evidence scoped to the single Redwood platform instance?

2) Assertion granularity: For CCM controls that touch key management and encryption-at-rest (e.g., CCM-HK-01 style items), do you provide a global KMS architecture diagram plus tenant-access lists, or do we need per-tenant key usage logs?

3) Sampling: For the audit, our external assessor prefers a 30-day sample window. Can you confirm whether you can pull a 30-day KV/transaction trace for a tenant scope if we provide dates?

We'd like to lock scope by EOD Friday so procurement can start DocuSign for the NDA / DPA. If helpful I can drop a quick checklist to speed the artifact handoff.

Appreciate it,
Ron
Security Lead — Atlas Health
[Attachment: initial_caiq_questions.pdf (pdf, 12KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ronald Hart <security@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 May 2028 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: CAIQ tenant scoping question and sample request

Ron —

Thanks, very useful set of questions. Short answers up front:

- Tenant isolation: Redwood's runtime emits both global platform telemetry and tenant-scoped artifacts. For CAIQ purposes we typically provide a platform-level control narrative plus tenant-scoped log excerpts for controls that are tenant-dependent (authentication/authorization, access logs, and KV access traces).

- Assertion granularity: Global KMS architecture + per-tenant key access logs is our standard delivery when customers require tenant-separated evidence. We do not create separate KMS instances per tenant by default.

- Sampling: We can extract a 30-day sample window for a named tenant; we'll need the exact tenant ID(s) and the date range. There are SLA/retention implications if you request older than 90 days — we will note that for evidence preservation.

Action items I propose:
1) If you can confirm tenant IDs and the audit window we'll provision exports.
2) We'll assemble a short assertion pack (control-by-control) and a tenant scope matrix to show which artifacts are tenant-specific vs global.
3) DocuSign path: once scope is agreed we'll send a limited DPA addendum and the evidence transfer playbook link.

I'll loop in Kim to pick owners and timeline.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]
